## Creating rxode2 models

The recommended way to write an `rxode2` model is a model function
with an `ini({})` block (parameter values) and a `model({})` block
(equations):

``` r
library(rxode2)
one.compartment <- function() {
  ini({
    tka <- 0.45 # Log Ka
    tcl <- 1 # Log Cl
    tv <- 3.45    # Log V
    eta.ka ~ 0.6
    eta.cl ~ 0.3
    eta.v ~ 0.1
    add.sd <- 0.7
  })
  model({
    ka <- exp(tka + eta.ka)
    cl <- exp(tcl + eta.cl)
    v <- exp(tv + eta.v)
    d/dt(depot) = -ka * depot
    d/dt(center) = ka * depot - cl / v * center
    cp = center / v
    cp ~ add(add.sd)
  })
}

# parse the model into a rxode2 ui object
mod <- one.compartment() # or rxode2(one.compartment)
```

The parameter values in `ini({})` are used when solving, so the model
can be solved directly with `rxSolve(mod, events)`.  Initial
conditions of the states can be set in the model block with
`state(0) <- value`.

Calling the function creates a parsed `rxode2` user interface object
(`rxUi`) which is translated into an `rxode2` compiled model when
solved:

``` r
mod$simulationModel

# or
mod$simulationIniModel
```

This is the same type of function required for `nlmixr2` estimation
and can be extended and modified by model piping.  For this reason it
is the form used throughout the documentation.

The model equations can also be given directly to `rxode2()`, without
an `ini({})` block:

- a `rxode2({})` block of statements;
- a `rxode2("")` character string;
- a file, `rxode2(filename="modelFile.rxode2")`.

These low-level forms create an `rxode2` compiled model object; the
parameters are then supplied when solving with `params=`.  See
<https://nlmixr2.github.io/rxode2/articles/rxode2-classic-models.html>
for these forms and when to use them.
